items.authors: Shavkat Karshiboev, Bobur Turimov, Sulton Usanov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov, Chengxun Yuan, Hasanova Sumanbar, Gulhayo Hayitova
items.abstract: Spinning test particles provide a precision probe of strong-field gravity, yet their dynamics around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity remain poorly constrained. items.title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
items.authors: Damianos Iosifidis
items.abstract: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.

We compute circular orbits on the equatorial plane, the prograde photon sphere, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). items.authors: Nattar Gayathri S, Zinnat Hassan, Uday Nambeesan, Saddam Hossain

items.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
items.authors: Karim Benakli
items.abstract: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

items.authors: Beno\^it Assi, Adam Martin

The models contain all 674 baryon-number-conserving operators, with minimal flavour violation for the fermionic operators, and are also provided in the Murphy basis. items.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
items.authors: Dongwook Ghim, Juno Kwon, Rak-Kyeong Seong
items.abstract: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

We establish the consistency of the orbifold conformal field theory, including the validity of operator interpretation. items.title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
items.authors: A. Ramesh Chandra

items.authors: Muxin Han

items.authors: Bruno Bucciotti
items.abstract: Static Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes vanish at linear and quadratic order in General Relativity, while generic nonlinear tides remain less understood. items.abstract: We study a version of the so-called D234 fermion action. On top of non-perturbative improvement to $\mathcal{O}(a)$, this action is also tree-level improved at $\mathcal{O}(a^2)$. items.authors: Miguel Gonz\'alez Albert, Ariel Arza, Saarik Kalia
items.abstract: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. items.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
items.authors: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber
items.abstract: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.

items.title: Charm and beauty production in pp collisions with ALICE
items.authors: Jianhui Zhu
items.abstract: Measurements of charm and beauty production in proton--proton (pp) collisions provide crucial tests of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) and unique access to heavy-quark hadronisation. In this contribution, a selection of recent ALICE results, with emphasis on LHC Run 3 measurements, is presented. items.title: Concerning Factorization at Lepton Colliders
items.authors: Patrick Hager, Dominik Schwienbacher
items.abstract: We uncover super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders. They arise from Glauber interactions involving colored partons produced by electromagnetic splittings of the incoming leptons. A three-loop analysis establishes the resulting factorization breaking, which we reconcile with the use of lepton PDFs below the soft veto scale. We conjecture that soft--collinear factorization fails for exclusive observables even in pure QED by identifying a genuine Glauber region in massless QED. This reveals a far richer infrared structure than naively expected.

items.authors: Nicolas Regnault (on behalf of the LEMAITRE project)
items.abstract: Recent BAO, CMB, and Type Ia supernova constraints on the dark-energy equation of state show a tension with the cosmological-constant model at the heart of $\Lambda$CDM, partly driven by low-redshift supernova measurements. We present the LEMAITRE project, a new measurement of the dark energy equation of state, based on a distinct SN~Ia dataset (2800 from ZTF, 170 from SNLS and 300 from HSC), a dedicated calibration program, and a new, independent analysis pipeline.

items.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
items.authors: Glenn Barnich
items.abstract: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

items.abstract: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. items.abstract: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. items.authors: Nina Elkina, Alexander Pukhov
items.abstract: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel.
